questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bentham and Hooker have given the classification of flowering plants. This classification system was
questions.solution: A natural classification system is based on natural affinities among the organisms and consider, not only the external features, but also internal features, like ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology, and phytochemistry. Such a classification for flowering plants was given by George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match column-I with column-II and choose the correct option.
 
  Column-I   Column-II
A. Phaeophyceae I. Funaria, Polytrichum, Sphagnum
B. Rhodophyceae II. Equisetum, Psilotum, Pteris
C. Mosses III. Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria
D. Pteridophytes IV. Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria
options: A - III; B - IV; C - I; D - II
A - IV; B - III; C - I; D - II
A - IV; B - III; C - II; D - I
A - IV; B - I; C - III; D - II
questions.solution:
Ectocarpus, Dictyota, and Laminaria are the members of Phaeophyceae or brown algae, which are found primarily in marine habitats.

Polysiphonia, Porphyra, and Gracilaria are the members of Rhodophyceae or red algae, while most of them are marine with higher concentrations in the warmer areas.

Funaria, Polytrichum, and sphagnum are mosses that are found commonly growing in moist, shaded areas in the hills.

Equisetum, Psilotum, and Pteris are pteridophytes, the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Fern prothallus is developed from
questions.solution:
In ferns, spores germinate to form a prothallus.
Ferns are known as homosporous plants. The sporangia are usually in clusters known as sori, found on the underside of the fern leaves. Some ferns have a covering over the sporangia known as an indusium. When the spores are mature, they are released from the sporangia. If a spore lands on a suitable site, it will germinate and grow via mitosis into a mature gametophyte plant (prothallus). A gametophyte is a plant that produces gametes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct description of the sporophyte of Marchantia and gametophyte of a fern is
options: Former is haploid while latter is diploid
Both do not have vascular tissue
Both represent the dominant generation in their respective life cycle
questions.solution: Bryophyta was the first land plant and both gametophyte and sporophyte in them do not have vascular tissue. Pteridophytes, on the other hand, were the first successful land plants with vascular tissue but in the gametophytes of pteridophytes, the vascular tissue is not present.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Pteridophytes, meiosis occurs in
questions.solution: The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells. The spores germinate to give rise to inconspicuous, small but multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chloroplast of Chlamydomonas is
questions.solution:
Shape and number of chloroplast in a different member of algae is different.
Chlamydomonas – cup-shaped, 1/cell
Zygnema – Stellate, 2 /cell
Spirogyra – Spiral, 1/cell
Ulothrix – Collar shaped, 1/cell

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Selaginella can be regarded as an evolutionary advanced Pteridophyte because of
questions.solution: Heterospory is the occurrence of two types of spore, smaller microspore, and larger macrospore. Heterospory has led to the evolution of seed habit in plants. Heterospory first evolved in Pteridophyta in which megaspore was retained on parent sporophyte which is considered as a precursor to seed habit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Nostoc is a
questions.solution: It is a prokaryotic organism belonging to the phylum of cyanobacteria. They are found in various environments like soil, wet rocks, lakes, springs, and rarely marine habitats. They form colonies composed of filaments of moniliform cells in a gelatinous sheath. Paracelsus coined the name Nostoc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Anisogamous condition is seen in
questions.solution: Sexual reproduction takes place through the fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. The fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Chlamydomonas is termed as anisogamous. The fusion between one large, nonmotile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following has the largest gametophyte?
questions.solution: Bryophyte has the largest multicellular free-living photosynthetic gametophyte. In Pteridophyta main plant body is sporophyte and gametophyte is small. In gymnosperm and angiosperm, the main plant body is sporophyte and gametophyte is highly reduced.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plants reproducing by spores such as mosses and ferns are grouped under the general term
questions.solution:
Eichler divided the plant kingdom into two subkingdoms: Cryptogamae-plants without flowers and seeds 
Phanerogamae-plants that bear flowers and seeds.
Cryptogams are further classified into three divisions: thallophyta, bryophyta, and pteridophyta. These are spore-bearing plants and commonly called as hidden plants which reproduce by producing spores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following correctly characterizes the plant body of Funaria?
questions.solution: The gametophytic generation represents the dominant phase in the life cycle of bryophytes. The sporophyte phase is dependent on the gametophyte. That is why, the plant body of Funaria is predominantly gametophyte with dependent sporophyte.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find out wrong statement regarding Cycas.
questions.solution: Cycas is an archegonial plant, in which female gametophyte contains archegonia. The archegonia are formed from the gametophytic cells lining the archegonial chamber. The number of archegonia formed in a gametophyte is variable among species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not common in Funaria and Selaginella?
questions.solution: A rhizome with hair-like root structures is present in Selaginella (Pteridophytes) and rhizoids are present in Funaria (Bryophytes).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Kingdom Plantae includes
options: Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms only.
Algae, Fungi, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms only.
Algae, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms only.
questions.solution: The Kingdom Plantae includes algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and flowering plants (angiosperms). They are common on land, on sea shore and in freshwater.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is grown to provide human food rich in proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals?
questions.solution:
Chlorella can be grown to provide human food rich in proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals.

Chlorella has been researched as a potential source of food and energy because its efficiency of photosynthesis can reach 8%, this is comparable with other highly efficient crops such as sugarcane. It is high in protein and other essential nutrients. When dried, it has about 45% protein, 20% fat, 20% carbohydrates, 5% fiber, and 10% minerals and vitamins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: From the point of evolutionary complexity, which one of the following is most advanced?
questions.solution: Pinus is a gymnosperm and is more advanced in comparison to algae, Bryophytes, and Pteridophytes. Main plant body is diploid sporophyte and gametophyte is highly reduced and not free-living independent structure. It is a completely successful land plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The organism shown in the given diagram is
questions.solution: The given figure is of green algae Volvox. The fusion of gametes is of oogamous type.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Adiantum belongs to the class
questions.solution: The pteridophytes are classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum); Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following, sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili is found
questions.solution: The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases, sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones (Selaginella, Equisetum).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The type of chlorophyll present in Phaeophyceae is
questions.solution: The major pigments present in the Phaeophyceae are chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids, and xanthophylls.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant group that produces spores and embryo but lacks vascular tissues and seeds is
questions.solution:
Bryophytes are the plants which produce spores and embryo but no vascular tissues are present, although the primitive type of conducting tissues are present in the form of hadrome and leptome.
•   Rhodophytes & phaeophytes are algae produces spores, no embryo & vascular tissue.
•   Pteridophytes have spores, embryo and true vascular tissues.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct regarding liverworts?
options: The thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate.
They are monoecious as well as dioecious.
Asexual reproduction by fragmentation or gemma cups.
More than one option is correct
questions.solution: The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid. The thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows on the stem-like structures. Asexual reproduction in liverworts takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialized structures called gemmae (sing. gemma). During sexual reproduction, male and female sex organs are produced either on the same or on different thalli.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bryophytes differ from Pteridophytes in
questions.solution: In Bryophytes, the vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) are absent. Water and nutrients enter the cell by diffusion, whereas in Pteridophytes, the vascular tissue is present consisting of xylem (without true vessels) and phloem (without companion cells).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is also called "amphibians of the plant kingdom"?
questions.solution:
Bryophytes are land inhabiting or terrestrial plants. They complete their vegetative phase on land but water is necessary for their reproductive phase i.e. for completion of the life cycle, so bryophytes are known as amphibians of the plant kingdom. Thallophytes have a plant body that is not clearly differentiated into roots, stem, and leaves. They do not have vascular tissue and hence are aquatic.
Pteridophytes are the most primitive vascular plants. They have developed vascular tissues and so they were the first vascular plants on land.
Tracheophyte includes all vascular plants - pteridophytes gymnosperms and angiosperms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In gymnosperms like Pinus and Cycas, the endosperm is
questions.solution: In gymnosperms like cycas/pinus, endosperms of female gametophyte are haploid and are formed before fertilisation. In angiosperms, the endosperm is triploid and develops after fertilisation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Gemmae are vegetative reproductive structures found in
questions.solution: Mostly bryophytes the vegetative reproductive structures are gemmae. Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Spirogyra, meiosis occurs during
questions.solution: Sporophytic generation is represented only by the one-celled zygote. There are no free-living sporophytes. Meiosis in the zygote results in the formation of haploid spores. The haploid spores divide mitotically and form the gametophyte. The dominant, photosynthetic phase in such plants is the free-living gametophyte. This kind of life cycle is termed as haplontic. Many algae such as Volvox, Spirogyra and some species of Chlamydomonas represent this pattern.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The number of chloroplasts in Chlamydomonas is ________ and in a mesophyll cell, it ranges between __________.
questions.solution: The number of chloroplasts is different in different cell types within an individual and it is different in cells of different species. Chlamydomonas has 1 chloroplast per cell, whereas a mesophyll cell of the leaf has 20−40 chloroplasts per cell on an average.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The fusion of male and female gamete in Chlamydomonas is called
questions.solution: The fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina is termed as anisogamous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the following which one is the example of Bryophyta that has elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal?
questions.solution: The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. The capsule contains spores. Spores are formed after meiosis. The mosses have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal. Common examples of mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum, and Sphagnum. Polytrichum is a genus of mosses - commonly called haircap moss.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Kelps and rockweed are examples of
questions.solution: The large (giant) parenchymatous forms of brown algae are called kelps or seaweed or trees of seas or forest of the sea. (e.g., Macrocystis 30–60m; Nereocystis 20–30m, Laminaria 2–12m). Both contain fucoxanthin, which is brown in colour. Due to which both are grouped under brown algae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Selaginella, male gametes are
questions.solution: Sperms (antherozoids) of Selaginella are 128-256 in number and biflagellated sickle-shaped (curved).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Analyze the given life cycle of plants and select the plants which represent such a life cycle.
questions.solution: The diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to the few-celled haploid gametophyte. This type of life cycle is termed as diplontic. An alga, Fucus sp., represents this pattern. In addition, all seed-bearing plants, i.e., Gymnosperms and Angiosperms, follow this pattern with some variations wherein the gametophytic phase is few to multi-celled.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following bryophytes provides a product that is commonly used as fuel?
questions.solution: Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Classification based on chromosome number, structure and behaviour is called
questions.solution: Cytotaxonomy that is based on cytological information such as chromosome number, structure, behaviour and chemotaxonomy that uses the chemical constituents of the plant to classify them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Oogamous type of sexual reproduction is found in
questions.solution: Oogamy is a form of anisogamy (heterogamy) in which the female gamete (e.g. egg cell) is significantly larger than the male gamete and is non-motile. Oogamy is the most advanced form of reproduction, with the egg cell or oogonium retained and fertilized on the parent plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a pteridophyte?
questions.solution: The Pteridophytes are classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum). Ginkgo is a Gymnosperm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Isogamous reproduction and flagellated gametes can be observed in
questions.solution: Sexual reproduction takes place through the fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Equistem belongs to class
questions.solution: Equistem belongs to the class of Sphenopsida of phylum Pteridophyta.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mannitol is the stored food in:
questions.solution: Mannitol is food stored in Fucus. Fucus is a genus of brown alga in the class Phaeophyceae and is found in the intertidal zones of rocky seashores almost everywhere in the world. Primary chemical constituents of this plant include mucilage, algin, mannitol, beta-carotene, zeaxanthin, iodine, bromine, potassium, volatile oils and many other minerals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Statement I: In Spirogyra, sometimes the gametes behave directly as zygospores without fusion. 
Statement II: In Spirogyra, asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia.

Select the correct option regarding both the statements.
options: Statement I is correct and II is wrong
Statement II is correct and I is wrong
questions.solution:
In Spirogyra, vegetative reproduction usually takes place by fragmentation or by the formation of different types of spores. Asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia. 

In Spirogyra, sexual reproduction takes place through the fusion of two gametes to form zygospores. These gametes are non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size, and sometimes the gametes behave directly as zygospores without fusion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Conifers differ from grasses in the
questions.solution: Conifers (gymnosperms) differ from grasses (angiosperms) because in gymnosperms, the female gametophyte is actually endosperm which is made before fertilisation. However, in grasses, endosperm is a tissue formed by the fertilization of second male gamete to polar nuclei. Moreover, in gymnosperms, the endosperm is a haploid tissue, whereas in angiosperms it is triploid.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The walking fern is named so because
options: Its spores are able to walk
It is dispersed through the agency of walking animals
It propagates vegetatively by its leaf tips
It known how to walk by itself
questions.solution: Adiantum caudatum is commonly called walking fern because its leaf tips when coming in contact with soil, form new plants as adventitious buds develop at leaf tips. This helps in the spread of fern over a large soil surface and thus, the name walking fern is derived.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Ulothrix, meiosis takes place in
questions.solution: Ulothrix is green algae which shows a haplontic life cycle, in which zygote is the only diploid structure and it undergoes meiosis to restore the haploid condition.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant body of Funaria is:
questions.solution: Funaria is a bryophyta in which the main plant body is haploid independent gametophyte, and sporophyte is dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition, partially or fully.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following plant cycles is exhibited by Ectocarpus and kelps?
questions.solution: The diploid sporophyte is represented by a dominant, independent, photosynthetic, vascular plant body. It alternates with multicellular, saprophytic/autotrophic, independent but short-lived haploid gametophyte. Such a pattern is known as haplo-diplontic life cycle. All pteridophytes exhibit this pattern. Interestingly, while most algal genera are haplontic, some of them such as Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, kelps are haplo-diplontic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cycas have two cotyledons but not included in angiosperms because of
questions.solution: In Cycas (gymnosperm) the seed does not occur inside a fruit but lies naked or exposed on the surface of megasporophyll.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is a non-vascular embryophyte?
questions.solution: In Bryophyta, xylem and phloem are not found, so they are called as non-vascular embryophytes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Statement-I: The mesophyll of Pinus shows no distinction as spongy mesophyll and palisade.

Statement-II: Parenchymatous cells are present in the mesophyll of Pinus.
questions.solution: Within the hypodermis of Pinus leaf is the parenchymatous mesophyll. It is comparted and shows no differentiation into palisade and spongy tissues. It consists of thin-walled cells which contain numerous chloroplasts and abundant starch. The mesophyll thus functions as the chlorophyll bearing tissue which manufactures food for plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following options about algae and their respective chlorophylls is correct?
options: Phaeophyceae - chl a, chl b and fucoxanthin; Rhodophyceae - chl a, chl d and phycoerythrin; and Chlorophyceae - chl a and chl c
Rhodophyceae - chl a, chl b and phycoerythrin; Chlorophyceae - chl a and chl d; and Phaeophyceae - chl a, chl c and fucoxanthin
Chlorophyceae - chl a and chl b; Rhodophyceae - chl a, chl d and phycoerythrin and Phaeophyceae - chl a, chl c and fucoxanthin
Chlorophyceae - chl a and chl b; Phaeophyceae - chl a, chl d and fucoxanthin; and Rhodophyceae - chl a, chl c and phycoerythrin
questions.solution: The members of Chlorophyceae or green algae possess chl a and b as their photosynthetic pigments. The members of Rhodophyceae or red algae possess chl a, chl d and phycoerythrin as their photosynthetic pigments. The members of Phaeophyceae or brown algae possess chl a, chl c and fucoxanthin as their photosynthetic pigments.

questions.q: Pinus is classified under Gymnosperms because
options: It produces seeds and it has narrow leaves
questions.solution: Gymngosperms are naked seed bearing plants in ovules remains exposed before and after fertilization. These  are non flowering plants in which ovules develops directly on megasporophyll.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a heterosporous plant?
questions.solution: Lycopodium is homosporous--all spores are roughly equal in size. Selaginella and Isoetes are heterosporous--spores are of two distinct sizes, microspores and megaspores. Salvinia and Cycas are heterosporous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mosses and ferns are found in moist and shady place because both
questions.solution: Mosses and ferns grows in moist and shady places as they are sciophytes and they require water for sexual reproduction. In mosses and fern male gametes or antherozoids are flagellated and they swim in drop of water to reach archegonia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Prothallus can be defined as a:
options: Dioecious autotrophic gametophyte found in pteridophytes
Monoecious heterotrophic sporophyte found in bryophytes.
Dioecious autotrophic gametophyte found in bryophytes.
Monoecious heterotrophic sporophyte found in pteridophytes
questions.solution: The prothallus is photosynthetic gametophyte developed from a spore in pterophytes, which possesses male and female sex organs for gamete formation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which plant group showed vascular tissue with integumented megasporangium for the first time?
questions.solution: Ovule is known as integumented megasporangium. Ovule forms seed after fertilization and first seed plants were gymnosperm hence ovule is seen for the first time in gymnosperm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Alternation of generation in bryophytes is
questions.solution: Bryophytes show the Haplo-diplontic pattern of alternation of generation. The dominating phase is gametophyte over which dependent small sporophyte is formed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is dioecious?
questions.solution: "Dioecious" and "monoecious" are terms that refer to the reproductive structure developed in a single organism. They are adjectives used in horticultural descriptions. Dioecious describes a plant group that includes distinct male and female plants. Monoecious describes a single plant that bears both male and female reproductive structures.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following plants, both pollen grains and seeds have a wing-shaped structure?
questions.solution: At maturity, the pollen grains are released from the male cones and dispersed by air currents. At this time, a pollen grain has two prothallial cell, a generative cell and tube cell. They form yellow clouds in pine forests. A pollen grain has two air sacs or wings for making it light. Part of the upper surface of the ovuliferous scale is peeled off along with the seed to form its wing. A female cone takes 26 months for reaching maturity. It further opens to release winged seeds that are dispersed by air. After falling on suitable soil, each seed gives rise to a new plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following belongs to Rhodophyta?
questions.solution: Polysiphonia is a species of red algae. Sphagnum includes members known as peat mosses. Polytrichum is a genus of the mosses which contain members commonly known as the hair mosses. Funaria are mosses belonging to the family Funariaceae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Common characters present between bryophytes and pteridophytes are
options: Possess distinct gametophytic and sporophytic generations and multicellular sex organs
Heteromorphic alternation of generation and rhizoids
questions.solution: The bryophytes and pteridophytes both possess distinct gametophytic and sporophytic generations, heteromorphic alternation of generation, presence of rhizoids, multicellular sex organs and require water for fertilization as their sperms are motile.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following does not belong to Pteropsida?
questions.solution: Pteridophytes are classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In fern, spores are formed in
questions.solution: The plants of pteridophytes are sporophytes. They reproduce asexually by forming spores in sporangia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The evolutionary important character of Selaginella is
questions.solution: Presence of two types of spores microspores and megaspores (heterospory) is the evolutionary characteristic in the life cycle of Selaginella.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these statements is correct about Eudorina?
options: It is a green alga and is isogamous
It is a green alga and is anisogamous
It is a brown alga and is isogamous
It is a brown alga and is anisogamous
questions.solution: Eudorina is a green alga belonging to Class Chlorophyceae. Their sexual reproduction involves two dissimilar sized gametes; hence, they are anisogamous.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Taxonomy based on the determination of evolutionary relationship is
questions.solution: Phylogenetic classification systems are based on the evolutionary relationships between the various organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is monoecious?
questions.solution: Pinus is heterosporous, monoecious plant, i.e., both male and female cones are present in the same plant but in different branches. Pinus produces micro- and megaspores in micro- and megasporangium, respectively.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Roots of which of the following plants are involved in nitrogen fixation?
questions.solution: Cycas shows presence of specialized roots called coralloid roots which are associated with the nitrogen fixing cyanobacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Selaginella is a pteridophyte which
options: produces micro and macro spores, has strobili and belong to the class Lycopsida
produces micro and macro spores, doesn't have strobili and belong to the class Pteropsida
produces only one type of spore, doesn't have strobili and belong to the class Lycopsida
produces only one type of spore, doesn't have strobili and belong to the class Pteropsida
questions.solution: Selaginella belongs to the class Lycopsida and is heterosporous since it produces one large spore and one small spore. These spores are borne on specialized leaves called microsporophylls which form distinct cones called strobili.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following groups would you place a plant which produces spores has embryo and bear leaf without vascular tissue?
questions.solution: First land plants are Bryophytes (Amphibians of plant kingdom) which lacked vascular tissue. They produced haploid spores by meiosis. The zygote formed after fertilization undergoes mitosis to form an embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The sporophylls forms a distinct compact structures called ________ .
questions.solution: The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases, sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones, especially in Selaginella, Equisetum. The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells. The spores germinate to give rise to the inconspicuous, small but multicellular prothallus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Isogamous condition with non-motile gametes is found in:
questions.solution: Fucus is a brown alga which shows oogamous reproduction. Chlamydomonas, Ulothrix and Spirogyra are green algae which shows isogamous condition, but in Spirogyra, the flagellated condition is completely absent in the life cycle thus it forms non-motile gametes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Rhodophyta are red in colour due to
questions.solution: Red-coloured pigment phycoerythrin is present in red algae along with chlorophyll a and beta carotene. Due to this pigment, they are capable of absorbing very low light intensity thus occurs in deep sea.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct statement.
options: Gymnosperms are both homosporous and heterosporous
The leaves of gymnosperms are not well adapted to extremes of climate
Sequoia is the tallest gymnosperm and is known as the father of the forest.
questions.solution: All gymnosperms are heterosporous. Marsilea is Pteridophyta but Ginkgo and Pinus are gymnosperms. Leaves of gymnosperms are well adapted to extremes of climate; they show xeric adaption and they survive for a few years.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If the endosperm of an angiosperm has 24 chromosomes, what would be the number of chromosomes in the megaspore mother cell of the same plant?
questions.solution: Ploidy of endosperm in angiosperm is 3n as it is post fertilization product formed by triple fusion and ploidy of mega spore mother cell is 2n.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements about Cycas and Pinus is correct?
options: The stem in Cycas is branched while it is unbranched in Pinus. The male and female strobili are present on the same plant in Pinus while they are present in different plants in Cycas.
The stem in Cycas is unbranched while it is branched in Pinus. The male and female strobili are present on the same plant in Pinus while they are present in different plants in Cycas.
The stem in Cycas is branched while it is unbranched in Pinus. The male and female strobili are present on the same plant in Cycas while they are present in different plants in Pinus.
The stem in Cycas is unbranched while it is branched in Pinus. The male and female strobili are present on the same plant in Cycas while they are present in different plants in Pinus.
questions.solution:
The main points of difference between Cycas and Pinus:
The stem is Cycas is unbranched, while it is branched in Pinus. Cycas shows coralloid roots with the symbiotic association with cyanobacterium Anabaena, while the roots of Pinus form mycorrhiza, which is a fungal association.
The male and female strobili are present on the same plant in Pinus (monoecious), while they are present in different plants in Cycas (dioecious).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Normally algae show a haplontic life cycle. Polysiphonia and Fucus are exceptions to this rule. The correct option depicting their classes and life cycles is
options: Polysiphonia is a green alga with haplo-diplontic life cycle and Fucus is a red alga with diplontic life cycle
Polysiphonia is a green alga with a diplontic life cycle and Fucus is a red alga with haplo-diplontic life cycle
Polysiphonia is a red alga with haplo-diplontic life cycle and Fucus is a brown alga with diplontic life cycle
Polysiphonia is a red alga with diplontic life cycle and Fucus is a brown alga with haplo-diplontic life cycle
questions.solution:
The diplontic life cycle is a cycle in which the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to the few-celled haploid gametophyte. It is seen in all seed-bearing plants gymnosperms and angiosperms. It is also seen in the brown alga Fucus.

Haplo-diplontic life cycle is a cycle in which a dominant, independent, photosynthetic, thalloid, or erect phase is represented by a haploid gametophyte, and it alternates with the short-lived, multicellular sporophyte totally or partially dependent on the gametophyte. This is seen in bryophytes, in the brown alga Ectocarpus and the red algae Polysiphonia

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pinus is a gymnosperm because it
options: is a large tree growing in colder areas
lacks ovary but possesses exposed ovules
questions.solution: The word Gymnosperm is derived from Greek words 'gymno' meaning naked and 'sperma' meaning seed. Thus, gymnosperms are naked seed-bearing plants in which seeds are not present inside fruits, as gymnosperms are nonflowering plants in which ovules are borne directly on megasporophyll. Thus, ovules remain exposed before and after fertilization.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In gymnosperms, the pollination is
questions.solution: In gymnosperms, pollination occurs by wind, i.e., anemophilous. During pollination, pollen grains land on the female cones near the micropylar region. The pollen grains are transferred directly to the ovule, as the ovules are exposed directly to the surface.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: <math><mtext>Which of the following does not have an</mtext></math> elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal?
questions.solution:
The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. The capsule contains spores. Spores are formed after meiosis. The mosses have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal. Common examples of mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum, and Sphagnum.

Riccia is a member of liverworts.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which group of plant kingdom gametophyte is depend on sporophyte?
questions.solution: In gymnosperm main plant body is diploid sporophyte which produces small gametophyte which is not free living and independent structure and is dependent on sporophyte for development and nutrition. Male gametophyte is pollen grain which is liberated after its germination and female gametophyte is endosperm which remain on sporophyte before and after fertilization.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In some Pteridophytes (Selaginella, Salvinia) sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones.
The Pteridophytes include Horsetails and Ferns
In Pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte
In Pteridophyta sexual reproduction is isogamous
questions.solution: In Pteridophyta sexual reproduction is oogamous in which multicellular and jacketed sex organs are produced. The male sex organ is antheridium which produces a flagellated male gamete and female sex organ is archegonium which produces single female gamete called egg cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In moss, sporophyte is formed on
questions.solution: Moss form the higher member of the Bryophyta having an erect plant body. In it, gametophytic stage is the dominant stage of life cycle having two stages - protonema and leafy stage. Protonema stage is also called as juvenile stage bearing buds from which the leafy stage is produced. It attached to the soil by rhizoids and bears the sex organs. The zygote formed by sexual reproduction develops into a sporophyte which forms on leafy stage bearing foot, seta and capsule. Sporophyte of mosses is more elaborate than that of liverworts.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding gymnosperms and choose the correct option.

I. In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes have an independent existence.
II. The multicellular female gametophyte is retained within the megasporangium.
III. All gymnosperms are heterosporous.

Of these statements:
options: I and II are true but III is false
I and III are true but II is false
II and III are false but I is true
II and III are true but I is false
questions.solution:
Gymnosperms are plants with naked seeds and commonly called as Phanerogams without ovary. These plants show heteromorphic alternation of generation where the sporophyte is diploid, dominant, independent while the gametophyte is haploid, recessive and dependent. Gymnosperms are heterosporous as they produce microspores in microsporangia and megaspore in megasporangia. The multicellular female gametophyte develops and stays within the megasporangium.

Cycas, Pinus, Ginkgo are classic examples of gymnosperms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which green algae shows only oogamous type sexual reproduction?
questions.solution: Volvox is colonial green algae and shows oogamous type sexual reproduction while Chlamydomonas shows all three type of sexual reproduction. Ulothrix shows isogamous type of sexual reproduction and spirogyra shows conjugation.

questions.q: Which is CORRECT for the fern Dryopteris?
options: Sporophyte is partially dependent on gametophyte
questions.solution:
Dryopteris a type of fern belongs to the class of Pteropsida. It is commonly called as wood-fern. It is distributed widely in all parts of the world with more diversity in the Asiatic region. In this plant group, the rootstocks form crown with vase-like ring of fronds (equivalent of a leaf). The sori in it are round and stipes have prominent scales.

It shows heteromorphic alternation of generation where the sporophyte is dominant and independent. The gametophyte is haploid and independent as well and it reproduces sexually.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Advanced oogamous sexual reproduction is found in:
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution:
Oogamy is the form of sexual reproduction and it is a type of heterogamy. Also comes under the part of anisogamy. Oogamy is the fertilization process where the male gamete is received by the female and fusion occurs within the female gamete cell.

In it, the male and female gamete are not of same size and shape.

Such type of reproductive fertilization is observed in Gymnosperm, Bryophytes, and even Pteridophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following four statements and choose the correct option based on whether they are RIGHT or WRONG.

(I) The sporophyte in liverworts is more elaborate than in mosses.
(II) Salvinia is heterosporous.
(III) The life cycle in all seed-bearing plants is diplontic.
(IV) In Pinus, male and female cones are borne on different trees.
questions.solution:
Salvinia is a genera of Pteridophyte which produces two types of spores - micro and macro. Such type of spores are called heterosporous. The microspore gives rise to male plant and the megaspore forms the female plant.

Liverworts, type of bryophytes, usually grow in moist shady habitats and its plant body is called as thalloid. The sporophyte of liverworts is differentiated into foot, setae and capsule. Mosses are another type of bryophyte whose sporophyte stage has similar three parts like liverworts but more elaborated.

Gymnosperms are heterosporous and the spores are made in sporangia that are borne on sporophylls called stobili or cones. Male cones are the ones bearing the male gametes and female cone bears female gamete. In Pinus, both the cones are found on the same tree unlike in Cycas.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What of the following is/are correct about Cycas?
options: Cycas has characteristic branched stems and pinnate leaves.
It is a dioecious plant, where male cones and megasporophylls bear on different trees.
Mycorrhizal associations are commonly found in the roots of Cycas.
questions.solution:
Cycas, a small-sized tropical gymnosperm is a dioecious plant. In this microsporophyll are organized to form male cones are present on one plant and megasporophylls are organized on a different plant. Thus, male and female plants are different in Cycas.
Roots in Cycas have small specialised roots called coralloid roots are associated with N2 - fixing cyanobacteria. The stems are unbranched. Pinnate leaves persist for a few years.

Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms but not bryophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Gymnosperms are named so because of the presence of
questions.solution: Gymnos: naked and sperma ; seed, thus gymnosperms are naked seed bearing plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remains exposed, both before and after fertilization. The seeds that develops post fertilization are not covered, are naked.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The ovule is absent in:
questions.solution: Gymnosperm (gymnos - naked and Sperma - seed) are plants in which ovules are not enclosed by ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization. The seeds that develop post-fertilization are not covered, are naked. This is a very important character of gymnosperm. In angiosperms, the ovules are present inside the ovary attached to the placenta. Pteridophytes do not have ovules. Meiospores are formed inside sporangia. Depending upon spore differentiation plants are homosporous (similar spores) and heterosporous (with two type of spores), smaller male microspores and larger female megaspores. Sporangia are associated with leaves called sporophylls.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: Brown algae has chlorophyll a and c, and fucoxanthin
Archegonia are found in Bryophyta, pteridophyta and gymnosperm.
The red algae usually reproduces vegetatively by fragmentation
Fusion of two gametes of similar size takes place as in species of Eudorina.
questions.solution: Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, nonmotile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The life cycle pattern of spermatophytes is:
questions.solution: Spermatophyta are seed-bearing plants which include gymnosperms and angiosperms. In spermatophyte, the type wherein the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to few-celled haploid gametophyte. This kind of life cycle is termed as diplontic. An alga, Fucus sp., represents this pattern. In addition, all seed bearing plants i.e., gymnosperms and angiosperms, follow this pattern with some variations, wherein, the gametophytic phase is few to multi-celled.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of heterosporous pteridophyte?
questions.solution: Pteridophytes divided into four classes- Psilopsida, Lycopsida (club mosses), Sphenopsida (horse tails) and Pteropsida or Filicinae (ferns). questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ulothrix and Spirogyra are:
questions.solution:
Ulothrix and Spirogyra belong to the class Chlorophyceae, commonly called green algae. Ulothrix, found in freshwater and marine water, is generally found attached to the bed of water bodies. The cells are very long and broad and favour low temperature for growth. They attach themselves to the bed by a modified holdfast cell. Spirogyra on the other hand a free-living and form mass floating on surface of water bodies. They are generally found in freshwater region and named so due to their spiral form of chloroplast.

Both these groups of organisms from filaments of chain of cells and are unbranched. Both show vegetative reproduction by fragmentation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Recognise the figure and find out the CORRECT matching:
options: a-Haplontic life cycle, b-diplontic life cycle, c-haplodiplontic life cycle
a-Haplodiplontic life cycle, b-diplontic life cycle, c-haplontic life cycle
a-Diplontic life cycle, b-haplodiplontic life cycle, c-haplontic life cycle
a-Haplontic life cycle, b-haplodiplontic life cycle, c-diplontic life cycle
questions.solution:
The alternation of the two phases of life cycle between sexual phase and asexual phase is called alternation of generation. Such life cycle pattern is commonly observed in plants and algae. It is also called metagenesis and in it haploid gametophytic (generally sexual) generation alternates with diploid sporophytic (generally asexual) generation.

There are three variations in the life cycle. In diplontic life cycle, the sporophyte is diploid, dominant, autotrophic and independent. The gametophytic generation is haploid, recessive and dependent on sporophyte. The duration of sporophyte is longer than gametophyte generation. Observed in Angiosperms.

In haplontic life cycle, the gametophyte stage is dominant, green, haploid and independent while the sporophyte stage is diploid, recessive and partially dependent on gametophyte. Also, the gametophytic stage duration is longer than the sporophytic stage. Observed in algae.

In haplodiplontic life cycle, both the stages have nearly equal duration and none of them are dominant. Gametophyte is represented as independent, autotrophic and haploid. Whereas the sporophyte is independent, autotrophic and diploid. Pteridophytes show such life cycle.

questions.solution:
The brown algae group, Phaeophyceae, is primarily found in the marine habitats and show a lot of variation in size and form. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids, and xanthophylls. They vary in color of various shades of brown based on the amount of fucoxanthin and xanthophyll pigments present in them. The storage form of carbohydrates in them are laminarin or mannitol.

Rhodophyceae is a group of algae, also called as red algae. They are majorly found in the marine habitat having a warmer climate. They are red in color due to a higher concentration of red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. They also have chlorophyll a and d. Food is stored as Floridian starch similar to amylopectin and glycogen. They generally reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation.

Chlorophyceae, also known as green algae, have a plant body that may be unicellular, colonial, or filamentous. They appear grass green in colour due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and b. The majority of them have storage bodies called pyrenoids in chloroplasts.

The haploid gametophyte alternates with the diploid saprophyte in the sexual lifecycle which is halodiplontic. The spore develops into mature gametophyte bearing archegonia and antheridia. Antheridia bears male gametes that swim to the female egg and fuse to form sporophyte. Foot, setae, and capsule form parts of the sporophyte. Haploid spores are formed in the capsule by the meiosis division process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sexual reproduction is of isogamous, anisogamous and oogamous type in:
questions.solution:
Chlorophyceae:
The sexual reproduction shows considerable variation in the type and formation of sex cells and it may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Some commonly found green algae are Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara.

Phaeophyceae:
Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Union of gametes may take place in water or within the oogonium (oogamous species). The gametes are pyriform (pear-shaped) and bear two laterally attached flagella. The common forms are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus.

Rhodophyceae:
They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes. Sexual reproduction is oogamous and accompanied by complex post fertilisation developments. The common members are Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria and Gelidium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Pinus, gametophytic generation is represented by
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution:
The gymnosperms are heterosporous; they produce haploid microspores and megaspores. The two kinds of spores are produced within sporangia that are borne on sporophylls which are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact strobili or cones. The strobili bearing microsporophylls and microsporangia are called microsporangiate or male strobili. The microspores develop into a male gametophytic generation which is highly reduced and is confined to only a limited number of cells. This reduced gametophyte is called a pollen grain. The development of pollen grains take place within the microsporangia. The cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules or megasporangia are called macrosporangiate or female strobili. The male or female cones or strobili may be
borne on the same tree like in Pinus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Angiosperms have dominated the land flora primarily because of their
options: Property of producing large number of seeds
Power of adaptability in diverse habitat
questions.solution: Angiosperms are highly evolved and well adapted land plants. They have both vessels and tracheids in xylem for better conduction of water. Roots are modified into tap root adventitious roots, pneumatophores etc. to suit the desire climate. Sex organs are highly developed, sporophylls and organized into flowers and the flowers the highly coloured or modified to attract pollinators at different times and places. The flowers are made attractive to attract a variety of insects. Flowering plants (angiosperms) have the exploited insects, birds and several other animals as agem of pollination, fruits and seed dispersal. It is one major reason for present day dominance of flowering plants. Seed are more protected as they are enclosed inside a fruit. All these adaptations have made angiosperms most adaptive in diverse habitats.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Peat moss is used as packing material for the shipment of flowers and live plants to distant places because
questions.solution: Bryophytes include mosses and liverworts. Peat is the deposition formed when there is a partial decomposition of organic matter. The moss, Sphagnum provides peat which is used as a fuel as well as a packing material for transport of living matter. It is used for the shipment of living materials as it can hold water and therefore keeps the live plants and flowers fresh.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following algae is used to prepare culture medium to grow microbe?
questions.solution: Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are among the 70 species of marine algae used as food. Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids (water-holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae) and carrageen (red algae) which are used commercially. Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria are used to grow microbes and in preparations of ice-creams and jellies. Chlorella a unicellular alga rich in proteins is used as food supplement even by space travellers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Water is not required for the act of fertilization in:
questions.solution: In spermatophytes, pollen tubes are developed to carry the male gametes to the egg cells for fertilization. In bryophytes, pteridophytes and cryptogams the male gametes are motile and therefore swim in the watery medium (external water) to reach the female gametes, the fusion of which result in fertilization.

Scutellum, Reticulate venation, Fibrous roots, Stilt roots, Pulvinous leaf base, Isobilateral leaves
questions.solution: Monocot plants are group of Angiosperms that have a single cotyledon in their seed. These plants have a fibrous root system (adventitious) which develop from the plumule. The leaves have parallel venation with stomata on both surfaces and vascular bundles are both - small and large. The leaves are isobilateral as both surfaces appear similar. The cotyledon of monocots are generally referred to as scutellum as they are thin and shield shape.

pear-shaped and bear 2 flagella that are laterally attached
pyriform and bear 2-8, equal and apical flagella

questions.solution: Phaeophyceae or the brown algae inhabit the marine environment. It is a very good source of protein and vitamins and is used as a food supplement. Ulothrix and Spirogyra are the filamentous forms of algae wherein the sexual reproduction take place with the help of flagellated gametes in Ulothrix and non-flagellated gametes in spirogyra. Funaria is a bryophytes with protonema stage
questions.solution: In the majority of the pteridophytes, all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The stems of gymnosperms are unbranched (Cycas) or branched (Pinus, Cedrus). The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The first stage is the protonema stage, which develops directly from a spore. It is a creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous stage. The second stage is the leafy stage, which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. Common examples of mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum, and Sphagnum. While most algal genera are haplontic, some of them such as Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, kelps are haplo-diplontic. Fucus, an alga is diplontic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the unique feature of bryophytes?
options: Reproduction only by the formation of gametes
questions.solution: They are the simplest and most primitive land plants and they require water to complete their life cycle. They are also known by the name of amphibians of the plant kingdom and are found in moist and shady places. They possess rhizoids to absorb water from the soil. The gametophytic generation in bryophytes is long-lived while sporophytic generation is short-lived so the sporophyte is completely dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition. Vascular tissue is completely absent in Bryophytes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not true for class Phaeophyceae?
options: Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation.
The protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus.
Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
questions.solution: Members of class phaeophyceae are commonly called Brown algae. In most brown algae asexual reproduction takes place by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella. In these algae vegetative reproduction takes place gfragmentation while sexual reproduction takes place by isogamy or anisogamy or oogamy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Among the following groups of plants, the correct set of archegoniate plants is:
questions.solution: Archegoium is female reproductive part of some plants. Plants having archegonium are called archegoniate. Bryophytes, pteridophytes and bryophytes have archegoium so they are included in archegoniate. This archegonium carries egg cell along with neck cell and neck canal cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct statement from the following.
options: Gymnosperm are both homosporous and heterosporous.
The leaves of gymnosperms are not well adapted to extremes of climate.
The giant redwood tree Sequoia is one of the tallest tree species.
questions.solution: All gymnosperm are heterosporous and produces two types of spores microspores and megaspores. Marsilea is Pteridophyta, Ginkgo and Pinus are gymnosperms. The leaves of gymnosperms are well adapted to extremes of climate. One of the gymnosperms, the giant redwood tree Sequoia is one of the tallest tree species. It is called the father of the forest due to its height.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The term protonema is related to some plants, which is :
options: diploid and is found in liverworts
diploid and is found in pteridophytes
haploid and is found in mosses
haploid and is found in pteridophytes
questions.solution: Protonema is a haploid structure found in some bryophytes (like mosses). In bryophytes after meiosis of spore mother cell, haploid spores are formed. These spores form gametophyte in which two stages are there <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo>)</mo></math> protonema <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mo>)</mo></math> leafy stage. Protonema is developed directly from a spore, and this protonema is creeping, green branched and frequently filamentous stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Phaeophyceae, the gametes are
options: pyriform and bear 2 flagella (one longitudinal and another transverse)
pear-shaped and bear 2 flagella that are laterally attached
pyriform and bear 2-8, equal and apical flagella
pear-shaped and bear 2-8, equal and apical flagella
questions.solution: Phaeophyceae or brown algae are the forms of algae usually found in the marine habitats with a wide range of varieties. The members of this algae, reproduce either vegetatively by fragmentation sexually with the help of gametes, wherein the reproduction may be either oogamous, isogamous, or anisogamous and asexual reproduction by the biflagellate zoospores which is pear-shaped and have two flagella unequal in size and laterally attached.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The life cycle of some plants do not involve a free-living sporophyte and the dominant, photosynthetic phase is the free-living gametophyte. This type of life cycle is called
options: the Haplo-diplontic life cycle and it is seen in kelp.
the Haplontic life cycle which is seen in Volvox and some species of Chlamydomonas.
the Diplontic life cycle which is seen in seed-bearing plants.
the Haplo-diplontic life cycle which is seen in bryophytes and pteridophytes.
questions.solution: In plants mainly three types of life cycle are seen (a) Haplontic (b) Diplontic (c) Haplo-diplontic. Haplontic life cycle is seen in most algae (like Volvox and some species of Chlamydomonas) and fungi. In which dominant phase is haploid gametophyte which is free-living and photosynthetic. Its alternate phase is sporophyte which is short living and is dependent on gametophyte. In Kelp and seed bearing plants diplontic life cycle takes place. In bryophytes and pteridophytes haplo-diplontic life cycle takes place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Fucus, the male and female gametes are
questions.solution: Fucus is a brown alga and it belongs to the division Phaeophyta. The thallus is flattened and small cavities called cryptostomates are scattered on the surface of the thallus. These cryptostomates have sterile hairs that help in the uptake of nutrients from the seawater. Fucus plant is a dioecious plant in which male and female plants are separate. Male and female gametes are formed in the conceptacle. Female gametes are denser than male gametes so they sink to the bottom and are attracted by sperm cells that will be motile.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bryophytes comprise of
options: a sporophyte which is of longer duration.
a dominant phase of sporophyte which is parasitic
a dominant phase of gametophyte which produces spores.
a small sporophyte phase which is generally parasitic on the gametophyte.
questions.solution:
In Bryophytes, sporophyte is never independent but is parasitic over gametophytic plant either partially for water and mineral supply or wholly for organic food.
The sporophyte is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it. Some cells of the sporophyte undergo reduction division (meiosis) to produce haploid spores. These spores germinate to produce gametophyte.
A dominant, independent, photosynthetic, thalloid or erect phase is represented by a haploid gametophyte and it alternates with the shortlived multicelluler sporophyte totally or partially dependent on the gametophyte for its anchorage and nutrition. All bryophytes represent this pattern.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect for gymnosperm?
options: Leaves may be simple or compound
In Cycas, the pinnate leaves persist for a many years
Thick cuticle and sunken stomata of needle-like leaves also help to reduce water loss
In conifers, the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area
questions.solution: In Gymnosperms, leaves are either simple or compound. In some gymnosperms like Cycas, the pinnate leaves persist for a few years. Leaves of gymnosperms are well-adapted for adverse conditions like to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity, and wind, etc. In conifers, like Pinus, the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area. Their thick cuticle and sunken stomata also help to reduce water loss.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Marchantia is
questions.solution:
Monoecious are plants having both sexes in the same plant and dioecious is a term used when the male and female reproductive organs are present in different plants.

Marchantia is an example of a liverwort, having a thalloid and whose male and female sex organs are produced on different thalli. Heterosporous are plants which produce two types of spores having different size and sex. Phanerogams are the seed-bearing plants or spermatophytes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Brown algae vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment:
questions.solution: The members of Phaeophyceae or brown algae possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Funaria antherozoids are:
questions.solution: Funaria is a moss which is a type of bryophytes. The main plant body of the bryophyte is haploid. It produces gametes; hence it is called a gametophyte. The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular. The male sex organ is called the antheridium. They produce biflagellate antherozoids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Diplontic life cycle is seen in ________.
questions.solution: Plants, depending on their types, show alternation of generations. In one type, the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic stage is represented by the single-celled to few celled haploid gametophytes. This kind of life cycle is termed as diplontic. An alga, Fucus sp., represents this pattern.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cyanobacteria is found in association with:
questions.solution: The coralloid root is developed in Cycas. It is produced in clusters at the base of the stem and protrudes out over the ground. It is dichotomously branched and greenish-brown in colour. It contains an algal zone in the cortex. This algal zone contains blue-green like Nostoc and Anabaena, which grow in symbiotic association with coralloid roots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Riccia, the female reproductive structures are called:
questions.solution: The sex organs in bryophytes (Riccia, Funaria), are multicellular and jacketed. The jacket of the sterile cell around the sperm and egg is an adaptation to a life on land. The male reproductive organs are called antheridia, and female reproductive organs are called archegonia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct statement.
options: The algal cell wall is made up of cellulose, algin, pectin and polysulphate esters.
Most of the gymnosperms are homosporous.
Most of the pteridophytes are heterosporous, and some are homosporous.
Water is not required for fertilisation in seed plants like Selaginella and Salvinia.
questions.solution: In Chlorophyceae, the cell wall is made up of cellulose. In Rhodophyceae, the cell wall is made up of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. In Phaeophyceae, the cell wall is made up of cellulose and algin. Gymnosperms are heterosporous, and most of the Pteridophytes are homosporous, and some are heterosporous like Selaginella and Salvinia. Both these plants produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores showing a tendency towards seed formation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these statements is true about Chara?
options: Oogonium and antheridium are present on different plants.
Oogonium is placed in the upper part and antheridium in the lower part
Oogonium is placed in the lower part and anthredium in upper part

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Pinus, male and female cones occur on
options: same branch of the same plant
different branches of the same plant
questions.solution: Pinus is a gymnosperm which produces cones bearing the male and the female reproductive gametes. The male cones are smaller and are found on the lower branches of the tree and the female cones larger than the male cones are on the upper branches of the same tree. Therefore the cones occur on the different branches of the same plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Prokaryotic autotrophic nitrogen-fixing symbiont is found in:
questions.solution: Cycas forms facultative symbiotic association with autotrophic nitrogen fixing cyanobacteria. Cycas provide fixed carbon and a stable environment to the cyanobacteria in exchange for fixed nitrogen. These cyanobacteria are endosymbionts and live within the roots of Cycas. In addition to normal roots, Cycas develops specialised symbiotic organs at a young age called precorallioa roots which transform into coralloid roots upon successful colonisation by cyanobacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which statement is true about bryophytes?
options: Spores form gametophyte plant on germination
questions.solution: In bryophytes sporogenic meiosis takes place i.e., spore mother cells of sporophyte undergo meiosis and form haploid spores. These spores on germination form haploid gametophyte. The main plant body of Bryophytes is gametophyte which is photosynthetic. A zygote is diploid structure which develops to form diploid sporophyte. Bryophytes ar non-vascular plants.
